newsitem.title: CANADA: CAI board move not seen affecting operations.
newsitem.headline: CAI board move not seen affecting operations.

text.p: Friday's resignation of all directors of Canadian Airlines International Ltd, the operating unit of Canadian Airlines Corp, was not expected to affect the operations of the struggling carrier, sources said.

Canadian said earlier today that CAI's board, which included AMR Corp chairman Robert Crandall and Don Carty, president of AMR unit American Airlines, resigned on the advice of lawyers to avoid personal financial liability.
"It makes no difference in terms of the day-to-day operation of the company, but it does remove them from any legal liability," said Ted Larkin, analyst with Bunting Warburg.
Canadian said CAI's affairs would be directed by Canadian Airlines Corp and Aurora Airline Investments Inc, the holding company AMR set up for its CAI investment.
